messages:
anya: Heads-up — Customer 'Streamly' reported consistent P99 spikes on the embeddings endpoint for small batches (1-4). They want predictable sub-50ms P99 for short prompts by next quarter. Proposing a focused 3-week micro-sprint to hit that: 1) small-batch kernel fusion path, 2) int4 quant fallback for embed models, 3) KV prefetch + aggressive prefix cache for short contexts, 4) batching heuristics tuned for low latency. Need owners, launch criteria, and canary plan.

matt: Can you paste the current numbers and the bench command you used? Also do we have signal that int4 won't regress embedding quality?

anya: Current numbers from host infra (avg across 4 regions): P50=18ms, P95=42ms, P99=120-180ms (tail varies by region). Bench command I used: 
```
./bench_embed --model redwood-embed-rt --batch-sizes 1,2,4 --iters 2000 --region us-west-2 --trace tail
```
Quality check vs fp16 on a 10k sample: cosine drop ~0.3% for int8, ~0.9% for int4 (single-run). Int4 risk exists for edge cases, that's why I recommended fallback.

rachel: +1 to micro-sprint. My priority order: (A) kernel fusion + small-batch fast-path (high impact, medium dev), (B) batching heuristic + kernel timeout adjustments (low risk), (C) prefix/KV prefetch (medium impact, infra work), (D) int4 fallback path (high risk, needs eval). We should gate int4 on embedding-quality-guard rails: automatic compare on rollout and easy revert switch.

matt: For launch criteria propose: P99 <= 50ms for batch sizes 1-4 in 3/4 regions AND no embedding quality regression >0.5% vs fp16 on evaluation set. Also require end-to-end tail budget (error budget) < 0.01% for 30d canary. Thoughts?

dave: From SRE side: we need a canary with traffic shaping and two rollback switches: model-variant fallback and traffic reroute to dedicated pool. We'll instrument extra metrics: kernel-failure-rate, quant-fallback-rate, kv-prefetch-hit. Suggested test matrix: synthetic low-latency load + real user trace replay for 72h. Timeline: 3 weeks dev + 1 week canary.

kate: Hosted vs Dedicated considerations: Hosted customers (Streamly) are on shared pools — risk of noisy neighbors. For this ask we should test on a dedicated small pool first before global rollout. Also confirm KMS and config flags for on-prem teams so Private customers can opt into same behavior.

perf-bot: quick-bench results (dev cluster): small-batch fusion prototype -> P99 58ms; batching-tweak -> P99 52ms; combined prototype -> P99 44ms. int4 prototype -> quality delta 0.8% on eval (needs more samples).

anya: Nice — perf-bot numbers are encouraging. Decisions so far: - Sprint scope: kernel fusion + batching heuristics + KV prefetch infra spike. - Int4 held as optional MVP behind rollout guard (only enable after automated eval pass). - Canary plan: dedicate 5% traffic on a dedicated pool for 1 week, then 25% for 3 days, then full. - Launch criteria: P99<=50ms for bs 1-4 in 3 of 4 regions, embedding quality delta <=0.5% vs fp16 on eval set, kernel-failure-rate < 0.01%.

Action items: - anya: create roadmap ticket + OKR link, add eval dataset (due EOD Thu). - rachel: owner for kernel fusion & batching (PRs ready in 2w). - dave: canary runbook + metrics dashboard (due next Wed). - matt: quality harness and automated compare + rollback flags (due in 10 days). - kate: test on dedicated pool and confirm Private config options (due next Tue).

anya: I'll convert this into a Q3 micro-sprint card and drop in the perf-initiative board. If anyone objects to scope or timeline speak now. :thumbsup:
